The `postgis/postgis` image provides tags for running Postgres with PostGIS extensions installed. This image is based on the official `postgres` image and provides Debian and Alpine variants for PostGIS 3.7.x, compatible with PostgreSQL 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18. Test images are also provided for PostgreSQL 19 pre-releases and builds from the PostGIS/GEOS/PROJ/GDAL master branches (`*-master`).
* By "cautious", we mean it does not always have the latest versions of geos, proj, gdal, and sfcgal packages.

Troubleshooting can often be challenging. It's important to know that the docker-postgis repository is an extension of the official Docker PostgreSQL repository. Therefore, if you encounter any issues, it's worth testing whether the problem can be reproduced with the official PostgreSQL Docker images. If so, it's recommended to search for solutions based on this. The following websites are suggested:
* search for the open or closed issues !
It's crucial to be aware that in a cloud environment, with default settings, these images are vulnerable, and there's a high risk of cryptominer infection if the ports are left open. ( Read More )

* Note that ports which are not bound to the host (i.e., `-p 5432:5432` instead of `-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432`) will be accessible from the outside. This also applies if you configured UFW to block this specific port, as Docker manages its own iptables rules. ( Read More )

Every `postgis/postgis:18-*` image includes `io_uring` capabilities for asynchronous I/O. However, some container runtimes (for example, containerd) have **disabled `io_uring` support** in the past due to **security concerns**.
If you wish to experiment with this feature, please do so **at your own risk**, and only after explicitly enabling `io_uring` in your seccomp profile.

**Arch Linux community package:** plainva in the AUR is maintained independently. Review its PKGBUILD before building; Plainva does not verify these community builds. The application’s licence remains AGPL-3.0-only.

Plainva follows a strict rule: **every file it writes must still open in Obsidian.** Notes are standard Markdown + YAML frontmatter; Plainva-specific presentation lives under a single namespaced `plainva:` key that other tools simply ignore. Existing vaults are never migrated or reformatted. The optional OKF conventions (typed notes, managed `index.md` files) are opt-in.

Note that the guarantee runs one way: Obsidian can always **open** what Plainva writes, but once a vault uses Plainva features (`.base` extensions such as boards or relations, managed `index.md` files), **editing** those specific files in Obsidian can break that functionality — Obsidian does not know the `plainva:` extensions. Notes without Plainva extensions can be edited anywhere, anytime. Details in the FAQ.

Plainva has no code-plugin sandbox — the vault *is* the interface. Every file is plain Markdown or YAML with an open, documented format, so any script, CLI tool or AI agent can read and write your vault directly and safely, with no Plainva-specific API to learn. See the guide's Automation & Scripts page and the machine-oriented file format reference; for AI agents there is a ready-made `AGENTS.md` template and skill. AI apps on the same computer (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, editors) can also read the vault through Plainva's read-only MCP server — no network port, folders granted per app — see Connecting AI apps. A direct write skips Plainva's pre-write backup — the version history only holds what Plainva wrote — so larger agent edits belong in a vault under Git. (A dedicated in-app plugin system remains a separate post-1.0 idea.)

**⬇ Download the latest release** — or, for OS-detected one-click downloads, use **plainva.com**. Every release page lists installers for all three platforms; updates after that are delivered in-app (signed, with an opt-out).

- **Linux** — the `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu) or `.rpm` (Fedora/openSUSE) for your package manager; the `.AppImage` (`chmod +x Plainva*.AppImage`, then run) is the fallback for distributions without a package. On a very new system the AppImage can clash with the host's graphics libraries — the packages never do; see Getting Started.

- **Nix** — community package: the flake in this repository wraps the `.deb` of a release (`nix run github:plainva/plainva#plainva-bin`). It is maintained by the community, covers x86_64 Linux only and is not built by the release checks; Nix, not the app, brings its updates. See nix/README.md.

- **Android** — the open test on Google Play: https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.plainva.app (tap *Become a tester*, install from Play), or the `.apk` attached to every mobile release. Android 8.0 or newer.
- **iPhone and iPad** — public TestFlight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/ZRSEfZBn. iOS/iPadOS 16.4 or newer.
